newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mosenergo CEO sees '97 profits down - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Mosenergo CEO sees '97 profits down - Interfax.

text.p: Regional Russian utility Mosenergo expects 1997 net profit to drop to 1.5 trillion roubles from 2.8 trillion roubles in 1996, Interfax news agency quoted chief executive Nestor Serebryanikov as saying.
A spokesman for Mosenergo 0#MSNG.RUO declined to comment on Interfax's figures but told Reuters the director had announced some preliminary data at a company conference on Thursday.
The agency also quoted Serebryanikov as saying pre-tax profit would drop in 1997 to 2.22 trillion roubles from 3.94 in 1996.

Mosenergo has not released 1996 results, but its net profit for the first nine months of the year was 1.96 trillion roubles after 1.55 trillion over the same period in 1995 and pre-tax profit was 2.77 trillion on 2.2 trillion.
Serebryanikov was quoted as saying this year would be "extraordinarily difficult" for the company, since electricity tariffs would not change much while fuel costs would rise.
He said that capital construction would fall to only 6.25 percent of the previously planned 2.6 trillion roubles for the year.
Mosnergo expected 315 billion roubles from the Moscow city government for construction and planned to use 200 billion in commercial bank credit at 48 percent annual interest rate.
Mosenergo planned to raise 624 billion roubles through a Eurobond issue, it said.

Serebryanikov said Mosenergo intended to reduce its energy outlays to other Russian utilities by three percent in 1997 as 30 of Russia's 70 energy systems owed the company more than 1.3 trillion roubles.
The company intends to produce 70.1 billion kilowatt hours in 1997, after 73.1 billion in 1996 and 72.1 billion in 1995.
